answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with stake-backed identity: a trusted kernel ties each public key to one locked bond, so splitting into clones never multiplies influence. An attacker who fills the orchard with fake nodes must post collateral for every new key, yet one honest agent's larger bond still outweighs them all. If cloning is found, slashing burns the lotus each clone staked, so cost grows per identity while payoff stays fixed and the flood turns unprofitable.
